exposure: Multiple embryo transfer (as a proxy for ART practice)
outcome: Obstetric complications (general mention in problem statement)
Birth defects (general mention in public health action)
Developmental disabilities (general mention in public health action)
cohort: The study cohort includes all infants born in the United States in 2018, with a specific focus on those conceived through ART procedures performed in 2017 and 2018, and compares their outcomes to all infants born in 2018.
finding: In 2018, ART contributed to 2.0% of all infants born in the US, accounted for 12.5% of all multiple births, and ART-conceived infants had significantly higher rates of multiple births (21.4% vs 3.3%), low birthweight (18.3% vs 8.3%), and preterm births (26.1% vs 10.0%) compared to all infants born in the total birth population.
mod_finding: The public health action section mentions that risks to mothers from multiple-birth pregnancy include higher rates of caesarean delivery, but this is a general statement about multiple births rather than a specific finding from the study data.
country: United States (including the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico)
cross-section timing: Data on ART procedures were collected for 2018, and birth outcomes from these procedures (and those performed in 2017) were compared with all infants born in 2018.
